catalog.location: Jezero Crater Delta (Wildcat Ridge / Skinner Ridge)
catalog.instrument: SHERLOC (Scanning Habitable Environments with Raman & Luminescence for Organics & Chemicals)
catalog.geological_context: Deep UV Raman spectroscopy revealed fluorescence emission peaks matching 1- and 2-ring aromatic organic molecules correlated with sulfate mineral grains in fine-grained mudstone.
catalog.biosignature_significance: Aromatics bound in sulfate and clay minerals are known on Earth to preserve cellular biomolecules from oxidation. Ranked by NASA astrobiologists as the highest potential biosignature sampled to date.

catalog.instrument: SAM (Sample Analysis at Mars - GC-MS and Evolved Gas Analyzer)
catalog.geological_context: Pyrolysis heating of 3.5-billion-year-old lacustrine mudstone to 850°C released diverse chlorinated and sulfurized hydrocarbons.
catalog.biosignature_significance: Proves complex organic matter has survived for billions of years beneath the Martian surface despite intense cosmic and ultraviolet radiation.

catalog.geological_context: Background methane oscillates seasonally from 0.24 parts-per-billion in winter to 0.65 ppb in summer. Periodic transient plumes spike up to 21.0 ppb (a 30-fold increase).
catalog.biosignature_significance: Methane has an atmospheric lifetime of only ~300 years on Mars, requiring an active modern subsurface source. Could be produced by active serpentinization olivine reactions OR deep subsurface methanogenic archaea.

molecules_detected: Black iron-phosphate rings surrounding white calcium sulfate veins ('leopard spots')
catalog.geological_context: Red rock stained by iron oxide was chemically reduced by organic-rich fluids, creating millimeter-scale circular halos containing iron phosphate and iron sulfide.
catalog.biosignature_significance: On Earth, this specific chemical redox reaction between organic carbon and iron sulfate/phosphate is a textbook fossil biomarker produced by ancient microbial colonies.
